newsitem.title: USA: Open arms greet Russian Eurobond traveling troupe.
newsitem.headline: Open arms greet Russian Eurobond traveling troupe.

text.p: Adoring global investors are proffering a bigger and more savory pot of honey as the Russia bear gears up for its Eurobond debut.
The roadshow from Asia to Europe to America has become more a celebration than a promotion, market sources said, referring to the last leg of the road show.
The New York bash is being held Wednesday at the Pierre hotel.

Given the progress Russia has made in economic transformation, its return to a pattern of responsible and moderate borrowiwng on the international capital market is cause enough for celebration, said Thomas Trebat, head of emerging markets research at Citicorp Securities.
"The degree of interest in Russia is entirely appropriate," he said.

The new kid on the block is being eagerly welcomed to the club by Latin specialists and money managers already entrenched in other Russian debt instruments. They expect enthusiam over the global bond to buoy their assets.

"It sounds crazy to compare Russia to Brazil," said Marcelo Fleury, head of Brazil Desk at Garban Corp, referring to the respective investment risks. But the fervor over Russia could enhance attractivenss of Brazil, he said.
To be sure, both countries are rich in natural resources and offer potentially large internal markets, but Brazil has a well developed infrastructure, while Russia's has barely begun, he said.

When Russia received a BB-minus credit rating from Standard and Poor's and Ba2 from Moody's Investors Service, some market watchers believed it put Brazil in a favorable light for an upgrade from its current B-plus and B1 rankings, respectively.

Brazil launched a five-year $750 million global bond at 265 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries at the end of October. The success of a Russian global with comparable tenor -- price talk now centers around 325 basis points -- would be nothing but salutary, Fleury said.
Citicorp's Trebat doubted the high tide of Russia's global bond would necessarily lift Latin debts.
The distinction of European and Latin markets in the minds of investors and rating agencies often defies logic, much to the chagrin of market players, he said.

A more apparent explanation may be found in the fact that Brazil has a much higher debt ratio than Russia. Investors can choose a wide array of Brazilian Eurobonds issued by sovereign and corporate borrowers, while Russian and Eastern European papers are scarce, he said.

Collectively, according to Trebat's estimates, Latin American countries will run up a current account deficit of $38 billion this year, compared to $5.0 billion for Eastern European countries and Russia.

Trading sources agreed that amid all the hype the market has largely kept sober, adding that the pricing should come close to 325 basis points for a five-year issue for $500 million. Talk exist of a larger size.

"We think the underwriters have managed expectations effectively," said one manager. "From the time of receiving the mandate, they have steered the expectations to 350 basis points even when the market was trading at 500 over at the moment."
J.P. Morgan and SBC/Warburg are joint lead managers.
"I don't see anyone hedging their bets," said another manager. "I doubt it could be a bust."
